claims.quote: Mutations in the γ-aminobutyric acid type A (GABAA) receptor γ2 subunit gene, GABRG2, have been associated with a variety of epilepsy syndromes.
A de novo mutation (c.T1027C, p.F343L) in GABRG2 was identified in a patient with early onset epileptic encephalopathy.

claims.object_text: spontaneous seizure activity and convulsive behaviors
claims.quote: Zebrafish overexpressing mutant human GABRG2 (F343L) subunits displayed spontaneous seizure activity and convulsive behaviors.

claims.object_text: hyperactivity during light phase with normal circadian rhythm; increased drug-induced locomotor activity
claims.quote: Tg (hGABRG2F343L) zebrafish displayed hyperactivity during light phase with normal circadian rhythm, as well as increased drug-induced locomotor activity.

claims.object_text: altered expression of GABAA receptor subunits
claims.quote: Real-time quantitative PCR, whole mount in situ hybridization and western blotting showed that Tg(hGABRG2F343L) zebrafish had altered expression of GABAA receptor subunits.

claims.object_text: robust synaptic phenotype causally linked to GABRG2(F343L) mutation
claims.quote: investigation of synaptic protein expression and synapse ultrastructure uncovered a robust synaptic phenotype that is causally linked to GABRG2(F343L) mutation.
displayed an unanticipated deficit at the presynaptic level
